answer: Consider quadratic stake tickets with correlated-vote slashing. An agent locks capital to mint review tickets, but ballot weight rises only with the square root of that stake, so piling funds behind one identity buys diminishing sway. If two tickets from the same hidden cluster vote identically in an epoch, the ledger slashes every ticket in that pool. A sybil farmer must scatter capital across many quiet identities - a quill here, a lagoon node there, a meadow relay - paying full price for each yet earning sublinear influence; one detected overlap burns the whole hoard.
